extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, patent drafters and applicants preparing European patent claims (EPO practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for drafting and amending European patent claims to comply with Article 84 EPC: clarity, conciseness and support by the description, and related formal requirements such as two-part form and independent claim limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must define the matter for which protection is sought
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 84 EPC requires that claims shall define the matter for which protection is sought.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The claim wording should enable the scope of protection conferred by the patent to be determined; purpose is legal certainty so the public knows what is covered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be clear
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be clear (the claim wording cannot be obscure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarity is judged with regard to legal certainty and should be apparent to the person skilled in the art from the claim wording alone; avoid context-dependent or ambiguous expressions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be concise
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 84 requires claims to be concise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should contain no unnecessary words or redundancies; conciseness aids legal certainty and ease of interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claims must be supported by the description
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims shall be supported by the description (support requirement of Article 84 EPC).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When claims are amended the description must be adapted carefully; inconsistencies between claims and description/drawings can render scope unclear and support must be ensured, particularly after amendment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Define protection in terms of technical features
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims must define the matter for which protection is sought in terms of the technical features of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claim scope should be expressed by concrete technical features rather than purely non-technical or abstract language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity must be apparent from the claim wording alone to the skilled person
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity must be apparent to the person skilled in the art from the wording of the claim alone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely on the description to cure an unclear claim; the skilled person should be able to understand claim meaning without resorting to other parts of the file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid relative or context-dependent terms (e.g., 'thin', 'wide', 'strong')
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative or similar terms such as 'thin', 'wide' or 'strong' constitute potentially unclear elements due to context-dependent meanings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If such terms are used, provide objective technical parameters or definitional context in the claim or ensure they are made clear in a way that the skilled person can interpret them reliably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional features must have technical specificity
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional features lacking technical specificity are a common Article 84 objection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When using functional language, tie it to concrete technical means, parameters, or structure so that the skilled person can determine the scope and technical contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid 'result-to-be-achieved' language without structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Result-to-be-achieved language without structure is a common objection under Article 84.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims should not merely state a desired result; include structural or procedural elements that define how the result is achieved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid vague references and undefined terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Vague references and undefined terms in claims give rise to clarity objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Define terms, use established technical terminology, or include measurable/qualitative limits so that the skilled person can apply the claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ensure consistency between claims and description/drawings
rubrics_metrics.description: Inconsistencies between claims and description/drawings could render the scope of claims unclear.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adapt the description carefully when claims are amended; maintain internal consistency across claims, description and drawings to meet support and clarity requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect the two-part form (Rule 43(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-part form must be respected: a portion indicating what is known from the prior art plus a characterising portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims in the two-part form should clearly separate the prior-art portion and the features that characterise the invention; failure to do so is a recognized clarity/formal objection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid multiple independent claims in the same category (Rule 43(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple independent claims in the same category are limited by Rule 43(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure independent claims of the same category are justified and conform to EPO formal requirements to avoid procedural objections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Article 84 not a ground for opposition except when amendment introduces non‑compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Lack of compliance with Article 84 EPC may not be used as a ground of opposition, but compliance may be examined when, and to the extent that, an amendment introduces non‑compliance with Article 84 EPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: During opposition proceedings Article 84 is generally not assessable unless an amendment creates a lack of clarity/support; practitioners should be aware of this timing when amending claims.
